subject: koala
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: koala gripping a eucalyptus branch stand.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
Looking at the render, the koala body reads as a messy rock-blob rather than a cohesive shape -- the faceted sweep geometry clumps the legs into the body and makes it disjointed, so I'm thinking a cleaner box-based torso with pixel-paint detailing would read much better.

The eyes are too tiny against the big nose box, so I want to bump them up to 3x3 with a highlight pixel; the arms are mostly hidden behind the body with just the hands visible on the branch, which is fine since the koala reads as sitting. There's a slight gap between the body bottom and branch A though, so the pose doesn't quite look like it's resting properly, and branch A itself bends oddly at the end with a post that looks more like a gallows than a tree limb -- I'll need to fix that stand shape too.

The gumnuts hanging off the leaf clusters look like they're floating randomly instead of connecting naturally, so I want to attach each one to its cluster with a small rod stem and drop the random offset. For the body itself, I'm switching from the ngon sweep (which creates a faceted rock look) to a box section instead, since that chunky blockiness matches the pixel-art puppet style better and will let the cell shading read more cleanly, including the cream belly patch.

Checking proportions: thigh sweeps, ears, and head-to-body width ratio all look fine as is, and I'll skip adding extra arm fur or a rump detail since the arms are mostly hidden anyway. For the eyes, I'm enlarging them to a 3x3 dark block with a highlight pixel, positioning them symmetrically around the muzzle so they sit just above its top edge — mirroring the left eye position to get the right eye placement correct relative to the face center.

I'm adjusting the eyelid shadow row to align with the new eye size, then reworking the gumnut generation to add a connecting rod and a bigger nut with a cap, making sure the random number consumption stays consistent so the rest of the leaf/cluster randomness isn't thrown off. For the body, I'm swapping the octagonal cross-section sweep for a boxier one and reconsidering the radius values.
